StackType.issue: The sim drops a re-application's offset citing PowerStackType.Single, which only means 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds regardless. DORMANT: Smoggy reads Amount nowhere (it afflicts with the literal 1). One of the 15 units making this misreading (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`).

AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: Same pile-limbo shape as power/ringing's matching entry: the sim walks `getattr(self.owner, 'all_cards', ())`, and PlayerCombatState.all_cards (player.py:100-103) is hand + draw + discard + exhaust with NO Play pile, where C#'s PlayerCombatState.AllCards includes Play (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80). Sharper here than for Ringing, because Smoggy's AfterCardPlayed sweep (powers.py:1748-1750) runs while the triggering Skill is itself mid-resolution: in C# that Skill is in the Play pile and IS afflicted with Smog, in the sim it is in neither all_cards nor the discard pile yet and is skipped -- so it can be replayed by an effect that returns it to hand, where the game would block it. PROMPT.md bug class 7. Reachable with any ported return-to-hand effect plus Living Fog. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.maps_to: powers.py:1768-1776 on_player_turn_end clears Smog and resets the flag
AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called for the player side at CombatManager.cs:1307 -- AFTER the turn-end card effects and the hand flush. The sim's on_player_turn_end is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (combat.py:654), before _process_turn_end_cards (combat.py:658) and before the flush (:661-662); the sim's real AfterTurnEnd slot, after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665), is available and unused. The concrete route for this whole group: StampedePower (powers.py:1025-1041) auto-plays Attacks from ITS on_player_turn_end, so in the game every turn-end auto-play happens while this power is still on the creature and in the sim that depends on registration order. Reproduce with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Note C#'s AfterSideTurnEnd here only CLEARS the afflictions -- unlike Ringing's and Tangled's, it does NOT remove the power -- and the sim matches that, clearing without expiring.

powers.py:1749 tests both. Smoggy never overwrites another affliction.

guards.what: SmoggyPower.cs:41 the history query on AfterCardEnteredCombat
guards.rationale: C# asks the history whether a Skill was played this turn; the sim keeps the `_skill_played_this_turn` boolean (powers.py:1729, set at :1747, cleared at :1766 and :1776). Unlike power/ringing's ShouldPlay, the flag and the history agree here: this hook fires when a card ENTERS combat, never from inside the triggering Skill's own resolution, so the start-vs-finish difference cannot bite. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because it is the same substitution that IS observable on power/ringing, and a reader comparing the two should see that the difference is the call site, not the technique.

guards.what: SmoggyPower.cs:66-70 ShouldPlay tests only `Affliction is Smog`
guards.rationale: powers.py:1760-1762 `not isinstance(card.affliction, SmogAffliction)`. Identical -- and note it does NOT consult the played-this-turn flag, because the Smog affliction only exists once a Skill has been played. Contrast Ringing, whose ShouldPlay must consult the turn state.
